- When sentiment is negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots downward in the next few days; apply a mild upward bias to counteract lagged sell pressure.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., dropping from 73+ to 65–68), model tends to underestimate the drop; increase downward bias in early forecast days.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often overestimates volatility; smooth out forecast curves to reflect lower expected noise.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period rallies; add a small upward bias in final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive or neutral.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes, model tends to ignore sentiment and forecast linearly; incorporate sentiment-weighted smoothing into trend adjustments.
